findings.output_locator: proposal.md lines292-305 (§6.4); witnesses.json W4; supplemental A/exec-h3g2pzcj/code.py lines10-18
findings.claim: Staging rows and merge_commit are written inside one transaction; absent marker after interruption leaves all staging rows available to quarantine.
findings.evidence: A W4 code/observed output demonstrates the uncommitted row disappears on close. SQLite WAL §2 describes commit by append of a commit record; SQLite atomic-commit introduction states all-or-none while expressly limiting that article to rollback mode. No separate durable staging transaction/journal is specified in the selected contract.
findings.reasoning: If new staging changes and the marker share the one transaction, rollback of that transaction also removes its staging changes. Therefore the proposed marker-absent/quarantine recovery branch cannot recover those rows as described. Precreated empty staging tables do not retain the rolled-back work.
findings.scope: Static source/contract inference, not a retest or claim that SQLite loses committed data. Restoring last committed state remains supported; separate persistent staging could be a legitimate future alternative but is not the frozen A contract.

findings.type: merge identity and deletion contract gap
findings.output_locator: proposal.md lines145-152 and268-275; supplemental A/exec-f4dz4zwa/code.py lines5-7
findings.claim: Edit identity is (record_uuid, rev_no); identical changes collapse and revision-based three-way merge keeps safe semantics.
findings.evidence: Two independently edited copies of the same record can choose the same next rev_no; author_device is stored but omitted from the declared edit identity. Toy function branch m==t returns base when both are None.

Static code inspection also shows that simultaneous removal of a previously populated field returns the base value, instead of preserving the identical deletion. That case was not executed in the three presented examples.
findings.scope: The exact three executed examples remain valid. This is a static counterexample/incomplete chosen merge contract, not an assertion that an implemented Fieldbook merger was tested.

findings.claim: R-tree contained-within expansion is applied in W2 design.
findings.evidence: The actual witness queries minX>=lower AND maxX<=upper and analogous Y bounds using unexpanded lon0±dx/lat0±dy. No rounding expansion appears.
findings.reasoning: The cited SQLite rounding rule is sound, but attributing its application to this executed witness is false. Equal hit counts on one random viewport do not verify boundary preservation.
findings.scope: Retain the index availability/query-plan/performance sample and the proposed expansion rule; no whole-app benchmark credit.

findings.output_locator: proposal.md lines133 and211; witnesses.json W3 corrected_finding; supplemental B/exec-n16mal6k/code.py lines12-20
findings.claim: NULL R-tree bounds remain NULL and never satisfy bbox constraints through SQL NULL comparison semantics.
findings.evidence: Witness inserts the NULL-bbox row, counts two index rows, and prints the exclusion explanation as a literal; it performs no bbox query or coordinate readback. SQLite exact version-3.46.1 rtree.c lines3013-3027/3130-3138 converts bounds through sqlite3_value_double; vdbeapi.c lines202-204 calls sqlite3VdbeRealValue; vdbemem.c lines658-672 returns 0 for NULL. Current R-tree documentation says nonconforming values are silently converted.
findings.reasoning: The all-NULL bounds convert to numeric zero; they are not stored SQL NULLs excluded by NULL comparison. A zero-containing viewport can match this row absent the application gate. The printed explanation is not an observed query result and contradicts the applicable versioned implementation.
findings.scope: No evaluator code execution/retest. Acceptance of the insert and rtreecheck ok are genuine recorded observations. Preserve the explicit has_geometry gate and visible count: these mitigate the product hazard but do not make the false source claim true.
